RP_001.characteristic: Hardness or softness — the quality of solidity or pliancy in matter.
RP_001.function: Acting as the supporting foundation for the other material phenomena in the same group (kalāpa).
RP_001.manifestation: Receiving — perceptible through bodily contact as hardness or softness.
RP_001.proximateCause: The co-arising of the other three great elements (water, fire, air).
RP_001.doctrinalNote: The four great elements always arise together, inseparably. There is no materiality in the immaterial realm.

RP_002.characteristic: Flowing or cohesion — the binding quality of matter.
RP_002.function: Binding together the material phenomena within the same kalāpa.
RP_002.manifestation: Matter is held together, not falling apart.
RP_002.proximateCause: The co-arising of the other three great elements (earth, fire, air).
RP_002.doctrinalNote: The water element is the only great element that cannot be directly sensed through bodily contact.

RP_003.characteristic: Heat or cold — the temperature quality of matter.
RP_003.function: Ripening and sustaining the material phenomena of the same group.
RP_003.manifestation: Matter is brought to maturity and ripeness.
RP_003.proximateCause: The co-arising of the other three great elements (earth, water, air).
RP_003.doctrinalNote: When occurring independently as external heat (utu), the fire element gives rise to temperature-produced materiality (utu-samuṭṭhāna-rūpa).

RP_004.characteristic: Distension or motion — the quality of movement in matter.
RP_004.function: Supporting and setting matter into motion.
RP_004.manifestation: Matter is supported and made to move.
RP_004.proximateCause: The co-arising of the other three great elements (earth, water, fire).
RP_004.doctrinalNote: In the practice of ānāpānasati, the breath (air element) is the principal meditation object.

RP_005.characteristic: Subtlety and clarity, capable of taking up visible form as its object.
RP_005.function: Serving as the physical basis for eye-consciousness to arise.
RP_005.manifestation: Eye-consciousness arises and sees the visible object.
RP_005.proximateCause: Past kamma; the presence of a visible object impinging on it.
RP_005.doctrinalNote: Produced only by kamma. Not present in the immaterial realm.

RP_006.characteristic: Subtlety, capable of taking up sound as its object.
RP_006.function: Serving as the physical basis for ear-consciousness to arise.
RP_006.manifestation: Ear-consciousness arises and hears the sound object.
RP_006.proximateCause: Past kamma; the presence of a sound object impinging on it.
RP_006.doctrinalNote: Brahmās of the fine-material realm possess the ear faculty because they communicate through sound.

RP_007.characteristic: Subtlety, capable of taking up odour as its object.
RP_007.function: Serving as the physical basis for nose-consciousness to arise.
RP_007.manifestation: Nose-consciousness arises and smells the odour object.
RP_007.proximateCause: Past kamma; the presence of an odour object impinging on it.
RP_007.doctrinalNote: Occurs only in the sense-sphere realm. Brahmās of the fine-material realm lack the nose faculty.

RP_008.characteristic: Subtlety, capable of taking up taste as its object.
RP_008.function: Serving as the physical basis for tongue-consciousness to arise.
RP_008.manifestation: Tongue-consciousness arises and tastes the flavour object.
RP_008.proximateCause: Past kamma; the presence of a taste object impinging on it.
RP_008.doctrinalNote: Occurs only in the sense-sphere realm. Brahmās do not eat, so they lack the tongue faculty.

RP_009.characteristic: Subtlety that pervades the body, taking up tangible objects (earth, fire, air) as its object.
RP_009.function: Serving as the physical basis for body-consciousness to arise.
RP_009.manifestation: Body-consciousness arises and senses the tangible object.
RP_009.proximateCause: Past kamma; the presence of a tangible object impinging on it.
RP_009.doctrinalNote: Brahmās of the fine-material realm possess the body faculty. It is absent in the non-percipient realm.

RP_010.characteristic: Appearance and manifestation — the object that is seen by the eye faculty.
RP_010.function: Serving as the object cognized by eye-consciousness.
RP_010.proximateCause: The presence of light together with contact with the eye faculty.
RP_010.doctrinalNote: Visible form (colour) is distinct from materiality (matter) in general.

RP_011.characteristic: Resounding — the object that is heard by the ear faculty.
RP_011.function: Serving as the object cognized by ear-consciousness.
RP_011.proximateCause: The arising of sound together with contact with the ear faculty.

RP_012.characteristic: Wafting forth — the object that is smelled by the nose faculty.
RP_012.function: Serving as the object cognized by nose-consciousness.
RP_012.proximateCause: The arising of odour together with contact with the nose faculty.

RP_013.characteristic: Appearance — the object that is tasted by the tongue faculty.
RP_013.function: Serving as the object cognized by tongue-consciousness.
RP_013.proximateCause: Contact of a flavour taken up by the tongue faculty.

RP_014.characteristic: The expression of femininity — influencing the entire material body.
RP_014.function: Determining the signs and behaviour characteristic of the female sex.
RP_014.manifestation: The expression of female sex-characteristics in the material body.
RP_014.proximateCause: Kamma that produces the female sex from the moment of rebirth-linking.
RP_014.doctrinalNote: Occurs only in the sense-sphere realm. Brahmās of the fine-material realm have no sex faculty.

RP_015.characteristic: The expression of masculinity — influencing the entire material body.
RP_015.function: Determining the signs and behaviour characteristic of the male sex.
RP_015.manifestation: The expression of male sex-characteristics in the material body.
RP_015.proximateCause: Kamma that produces the male sex from the moment of rebirth-linking.
RP_015.doctrinalNote: Occurs only in the sense-sphere realm.

RP_016.characteristic: Being the seat — the physical basis on which mind-door consciousness depends.
RP_016.function: Serving as the physical basis for all consciousness that arises through the mind-door (excluding the sense-door pairs).
RP_016.manifestation: Mind-door consciousness is able to arise.
RP_016.proximateCause: Produced by past kamma; sustained by the blood of the heart.
RP_016.doctrinalNote: Absent in the immaterial realm. This is the most important material basis in the Abhidhamma system of cognition.

RP_017.characteristic: Sustaining life — preserving the material phenomena produced by kamma.
RP_017.function: Keeping kamma-produced materiality in existence for the duration of one material life-span.
RP_017.manifestation: Kamma-produced materiality is kept alive and persisting.
RP_017.proximateCause: Only kamma can produce material life faculty.
RP_017.doctrinalNote: The lifespan of materiality equals seventeen mind-moments. When material life faculty ceases, the kamma-produced materiality ceases with it.

RP_018.characteristic: Nourishment — the nutritive essence present in every material group.
RP_018.function: Nourishing the material phenomena of the same group and generating new materiality from nutriment.
RP_018.manifestation: Materiality is nourished, sustained and multiplied.
RP_018.proximateCause: The presence of nutriment (food) that is digested.
RP_018.doctrinalNote: Nutritive essence in physical food (kabaḷīkāra-āhāra) is one of the four kinds of nutriment in the Abhidhamma.

RP_019.characteristic: Delimiting — creating the boundary between groups of materiality.
RP_019.manifestation: The groups of materiality are distinguished and do not merge.
RP_019.proximateCause: The presence of material groups (kalāpas) existing alongside one another.
RP_019.doctrinalNote: The space element as a material phenomenon is not the same as absolute space in philosophy.

RP_020.characteristic: Movement — bodily expression used to convey an intention.
RP_020.function: Communicating an intention through bodily gesture.
RP_020.manifestation: Others understand one's intention through bodily gesture.
RP_020.proximateCause: A consciousness arising with the intention to express something.
RP_020.doctrinalNote: Produced only by mind. It is the basis of bodily action (kāya-kamma).

RP_021.characteristic: Vocal expression — speech used to convey an intention.
RP_021.manifestation: Others understand one's intention through the sound of speech.
RP_021.proximateCause: A consciousness arising with the intention to speak.
RP_021.doctrinalNote: Produced only by mind. It is the basis of verbal action (vacī-kamma).

RP_022.characteristic: Lightness — the buoyant, agile quality of materiality.
RP_022.function: Preventing materiality from being heavy and rigid.
RP_022.manifestation: The body is light and moves with ease.
RP_022.proximateCause: Favourable mind, temperature and nutriment; freedom from illness.
RP_022.doctrinalNote: Not produced by kamma. Depends on present health and conditions.

RP_023.characteristic: Softness — the pliant, malleable quality of materiality.
RP_023.function: Preventing materiality from being stiff and rigid.
RP_023.manifestation: The body is soft and supple.
RP_023.proximateCause: Harmonious mind, temperature and nutriment; freedom from illness.

RP_024.characteristic: Adaptability — the workable, fit quality of materiality.
RP_024.function: Making materiality easy to use and free of fatigue.
RP_024.manifestation: The body is fit for any task.

RP_025.characteristic: Genesis — the initial arising phase of a material group.
RP_025.function: Marking the beginning of existence of a material group.
RP_025.manifestation: Materiality comes into being in the world.
RP_025.proximateCause: The four originators of materiality (kamma, mind, temperature, nutriment).
RP_025.doctrinalNote: The four characteristics of materiality are phases of all material phenomena, not independent material instances.

RP_026.characteristic: Continuity — the phase of persistence and duration of the stream of materiality.
RP_026.function: Keeping the stream of materiality continuing without interruption.
RP_026.proximateCause: The four originators of materiality acting continuously.
RP_026.doctrinalNote: Continuity explains why things seem stable to us — they are in fact an unbroken stream of arising and passing away.

RP_027.characteristic: Decay — the ageing, declining phase of materiality.
RP_027.function: Marking the change and decline of materiality.
RP_027.manifestation: Materiality grows old, wears down, and changes.
RP_027.proximateCause: The passage of time; materiality having already existed.
RP_027.doctrinalNote: Decay is the clearest visible sign of impermanence (anicca) in materiality.

RP_028.characteristic: Dissolution — the complete cessation of materiality.
RP_028.function: Marking the end of the existence of materiality.
RP_028.manifestation: Materiality no longer exists — it has completely ceased.
RP_028.proximateCause: Materiality having already passed through the three preceding phases of arising, persisting and changing.
RP_028.doctrinalNote: Clearly seeing the phase of dissolution is the starting point of insight meditation (vipassanā).
